audits.title: Audit of Clinic Letters Sent to GP Following CAMHS Outpatient Clinic Appointments at Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on writing clinic letters
audits.setting: CAMHS consultant outpatient clinics, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: ICD-10 diagnosis 80%; medication indications 32.5%; physical measurements 55%; mental state 60%; risk assessment 70%; current medication 100%; allergies 27.5%; useful links 7.5%.

cycle2.result: ICD-10 diagnosis 100%; medication indications 56.6%; physical measurements 80%; mental state 88.3%; risk assessment 86.6%; current medication 90%; allergies 3.3%; useful links 13.3%.

audits.other_findings: Copying patients or carers into letters fell from 100% to 86.6%. A QI project to collate useful links was proposed.
audits.citation: Afinni-Adewunmi N, Eneka-Akhator N, Manuwa O. Audit of Clinic Letters Sent to GP Following CAMHS Outpatient Clinic Appointments at Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S148-S149. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.401.

audits.title: Secondary Service Communications to GPs-a Regional Audit
audits.standard: RCPsych and PRSB recommendations for letters to GPs
audits.setting: Three psychiatric units across three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: Missing care coordinator details 91.7%, medical comorbidities 61.22%, non-psychiatric diagnosis 79.59%, actions for GP 71.43%; psychiatric diagnosis 83.47%, psychiatric medications and follow-up plan 80.17%.

audits.intervention: Local guidelines and letter template with recommended headings, and formal teaching for junior doctors

cycle2.result: Psychiatric diagnosis 97.1% (previously 83.5%), psychiatric medication 91.4% (80.17%), follow-up plan 98.6% (80.2%); medical comorbidity 28.6% vs 31.4%, non-psychiatric medication 65.7% vs 34.7%, care coordinator 54.3% vs 8.3%, action for GP 27.1% vs 44.6%.

audits.other_findings: Two headings declined and change varied between sites. Barriers were template not used, lack of junior training and psychiatrist workload.
audits.citation: Mitu T, Zachariah V, Ray J, Salmoiraghi A, Singh R, Williams L, et al.. Secondary Service Communications to GPs-a Regional Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S170-S171. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.449.

audits.title: An Audit of the Consistency and Quality of Letters From Choice Appointments in CAMHS South Edinburgh
audits.standard: Standards derived from the CAPA Book and CAMHS South Choice Handbook (12 letter content and process standards, including maximum two sides of A4 and sent within two weeks)

cycle1.result: Current concerns 92%, background 96%, patient goals 40%, clinician impression 62%, choices discussed 22%, choices made 100%, self-help agreed 52%, services required 100%, maximum two sides of A4 50%, copy to patient 88%, copy to referrer 100%, sent within two weeks 72%.

audits.intervention: Additional Choice training, electronic canned text for letters and collation of Choice guidance. Re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: 94 different resources were shared, from 0 to 19 per letter, suggesting variable individualisation.
audits.citation: Dempsey E. An Audit of the Consistency and Quality of Letters From Choice Appointments in CAMHS South Edinburgh. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S226-S226. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.555.

audits.title: Clinical Audit to Evaluate the Quality of GP Letters From Psychiatry Clinic at TEWV NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on GP letters (January 2021), 10 domains
audits.setting: Psychiatry clinics, TEWV NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.period: Letters September to December 2023; audited December 2023 to January 2024
cycle1.result: 100% for contact details, review date, consultation, participants and plan; venue and diagnosis 97%; medications 93%; care coordinator 60%; MSE 70%; risk 50%; user-friendly information 23%; allergies 13%; service users copied in 3%.

audits.intervention: Updated GP letter template with sections for allergies, risk, user-friendly information and copying patients; dissemination via huddles, trainee handovers, laminated copies and email
audits.citation: Ataria R, Fayomi S, Sugumaran H, Morgans C, Podmore S. Clinical Audit to Evaluate the Quality of GP Letters From Psychiatry Clinic at TEWV NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S219-S219. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10553.

audits.title: Assessing the Recording of Adequate Care Plans in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: BCHFT guidelines requiring a documented care plan covering 5 key criteria; GMC advice on contemporaneous records
audits.setting: Sandwell CAMHS, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.period: clinic letters from the past 12 months
cycle1.result: Medication information included in 79% when relevant; physical health considerations 36%; crisis planning 20%; 15% of letters had no clear 'Care Plan' subheading.

audits.other_findings: A standardised clinic letter template with a 'Care Plan' section and standard crisis contacts was recommended; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Choudary S, Yokoyama-King H, Ariyathurai A, Sivasubramanian K. Assessing the Recording of Adequate Care Plans in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S223-S224. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10563.

audits.title: Timeliness of Communication: An Audit of Clinic Documentation and Outpatient Correspondence Within Community Mental Health Teams
audits.standard: Trust standard (NHS Standard Contract): 100% of clinic outcomes completed within 24 hours and clinic letters within 7 days
audits.setting: North and South Community Mental Health Teams, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Clinic entries within 24 hours: South 99%, North 94%; letters within 7 days: South 99%, North 92%; 8% of North letters overdue or missing, some up to 31 days

audits.other_findings: Recommended presenting findings, an administrative capacity survey and a 12-week re-audit.
audits.citation: Gul A. Timeliness of Communication: An Audit of Clinic Documentation and Outpatient Correspondence Within Community Mental Health Teams. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S296-S297. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11712.

audits.title: Clinical Audit Assessing Compliance with GP Communication Standards Following Initial Assessments in a Community Mental Health Team
audits.standard: NHS Standard Contract (2022) and HSE National Clinical Programme for Mental Health (2020): GP letter within 14 days of assessment
audits.setting: CMHT Swords – Orange Team, North Dublin Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: 15 (75%) sent within 7 days, 4 (20%) within 8–14 days and 1 (5%) after 14 days; 95% overall compliance.

audits.other_findings: Only patients assessed by the auditor were included.
audits.citation: Murtaza G. Clinical Audit Assessing Compliance with GP Communication Standards Following Initial Assessments in a Community Mental Health Team. European Psychiatry. 2026;69(S1):S922-S922. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.11712.
